title: Faster eviction did not translate into a qualified serving optimization
summary: No new optimization qualified beyond existing wait hints. Large eviction calls sped up substantially, but eviction occupied less than 0.05% of primary/tight workflow time and only 0.09% in the larger-document diagnostic.
scope: 144 valid development cases plus two invalid configurations. Selected timing and pressure panels used three repetitions; exact-state CPU replay examined native decisions.
limitations: Development-selected inputs are not independent confirmation. Some mechanisms never activated, so their value remains unresolved rather than disproved.
decision: Keep the simple candidate. Preserve microbenchmark gains as diagnostics and require end-to-end value before importing faster eviction or inactive bridges.

chart.caption: Three-repetition development panels. Different candidate comparisons are shown separately; higher is faster.
